newsitem.title: USA: KLA Instruments, Tencor to merge.
newsitem.headline: KLA Instruments, Tencor to merge.

text.p: KLA Instruments Corp. and Tencor Instruments said Tuesday they will merge in a stock swap deal that would create a company with the most comprehensive measurement and analysis systems used in the manufacture of computer chips.
The combined company, KLA-Tencor, will have combined revenues of more than $1 billion and more than 3,900 employees worldwide, they said.
Under the definitive agreement, KLA will exchange each of its shares and options for one of Tencor's outstanding shares and options in a tax-free pooling of interests.
The deal is expected to close during the quarter ending June 30, subject to regulatory and shareholder approval.

The merger came as semiconductor equipment stocks have been rebounding from a cyclical downturn in mid-1996, when tumbling prices for memory chips due to sharply increased capacity and insufficient demand chilled the sector.
KLA's stock hit a 52-week intraday high of $41.625 before closing at $40.875, up 87.5 cents on the day. Tencor also hit a year intraday high of $31.25 before before closing at $30.50, up 43.75 cents.
The merger was announced after the close of trading in the Nasdaq market.
